OCCUPATIONAL FITNESS PLATFORM · EVIDENCE TO JUDGMENT

What changed in the evidence and the judgment?

Identical patient facts, model, options and system prompt. The evidence bundle and its order differ. This does not isolate the causal contribution of one passage or position. Engineering reference agreement is not clinical accuracy; independent support review is pending.

Completed frozen comparison; three independent calls per model/method. Pilot and full-run completion remain separate. No new model calls were made by this analysis. Exact paired records · Input versions

Completed retrieval-v2 judgment revision

Engineering reference agreement across 33 observed development cases; not clinical accuracy. Three independent calls are repeated conditions, not additional patients. Source identifier validity is distinct from explanation support. Evidence bundles and order differ; this does not isolate one passage's causal effect. The completed judgment revision uses retrieval-v2, not the later guarded retrieval revisions.

198 paired conditions: 33 cases × 2 judges × 3 independent calls. Validation failures stay in the all-recorded agreement denominator. Macro-F1 is computed on accepted outputs and observed classes, with failures listed separately.

3. AFTD2022-EXP-7f3c434bba3c53df

Section 4.3 · PDF 120 · Printed page 109 · Original PDF

Commercial standards
(Drivers of heavy vehicles, public passenger vehicles 
or requiring a dangerous goods driver licence – 
refer to definition in Table 3)
Compliance with the standard should be clinically 
assessed initially. If the initial clinical assessment 
indicates possible hearing loss, the person should 
be referred for audiometry.
A person is not fit to hold an unconditional licence:
•	 if the person has unaided hearing loss ≥ 40 dB 
in the better ear (averaged over the frequencies 
0.5, 1, 2 and 3 KHz).
A conditional licence may be considered by the 
driver licensing authority subject to periodic review*, 
taking into account the nature of the driving task 
and information provided by an ENT specialist or 
audiologist**, as to whether:
•	 the standard is able to be met with a hearing 
aid***.
If the standard is not able to be met with a hearing 
aid, further individualised assessment should be 
offered. 
A conditional licence may be considered by the 
driver licensing authority subject to periodic review*, 
taking into account:
•	 the nature of the driving task; and
•	 information provided by an ENT specialist or 
audiologist**; and
•	 the results of a practical driver assessment if 
required. 
* Stable conditions may not require periodic review. 
** Refer to section 4.2. General assessment and 
management guidelines.
*** In some cases, noise amplification as a result of 
wearing hearing aids may lead to driver distraction 
and may warrant individualised assessment to 
determine fitness to drive without the hearing aid 
(refer to 4.2. General assessment and management 
guidelines).
4. AFTD2022-EXP-2332d9548f2abd01

Section 1.2.3 · PDF 68 · Printed page 57 · Original PDF

1.2.3. Blackouts due to medical 
causes not covered in the standards
If the cause of the blackout is determined 
to be a medical condition not covered in 
the standards, then first principles regarding 
fitness to drive should be applied (refer to 
Part A section 2. Assessing fitness to drive 
– general guidance). Considerations include 
the likelihood of recurrence of blackout and 
the treatability of the condition as well as the 
nature of the driving task. There should also be 
an appropriate review period. A more stringent 
approach should be considered for commercial 
vehicle drivers.
5. AFTD2022-DM-COM-009

Section 3.3.2 · PDF 110 · Printed page 99 · Original PDF

3.3.2. Recommendation and 
review of conditional licences for 
commercial vehicle drivers
It is a general requirement that conditional 
licences for commercial vehicle drivers are 
issued by the driver licensing authority based on 
advice from an appropriate medical specialist 
(endocrinologist or consultant physician 
specialising in diabetes) and that these drivers 
are reviewed periodically by the specialist to 
determine their ongoing fitness to drive (refer 
to Part A section 4.4. Conditional licences). For 
commercial drivers receiving insulin treatment, at 
least three months of blood glucose monitoring 
records should be reviewed in assessing fitness 
to drive.

1. AFTD2022-EXP-f57fef6c660a1e6d

Section 2.3.1 · PDF 99 · Printed page 88 · Original PDF

Commercial standards
(Drivers of heavy vehicles, public passenger 
vehicles or requiring a dangerous goods 
driver licence – refer to definition in Table 3)
A person is not fit to hold an unconditional 
licence:
•	 if the person has blood pressure 
consistently > 170 systolic or > 100 diastolic 
(treated or untreated).
A conditional licence may be considered 
by the driver licensing authority subject to 
annual review, taking into account the nature 
of the driving task and information provided 
by the treating specialist* as to whether the 
following criteria are met:
•	 the person is treated with antihypertensive 
therapy and effective control of 
hypertension is achieved over a 4-week 
follow-up period; and
•	 there are no side effects from the 
medication that will impair safe driving; and
•	 there is no evidence of damage to target 
organs relevant to driving.
* Ongoing fitness to drive for commercial 
vehicle drivers may be assessed by the 
treating GP provided this is mutually agreed 
by the specialist, GP and driver licensing 
authority. The initial granting of a conditional 
licence must, however, be based on 
information provided by the specialist.
2. AFTD2022-EXP-a09b64ac70a92828

Section 10.3 · PDF 220 · Printed page 209 · Original PDF

Commercial standards
(Drivers of heavy vehicles, public passenger 
vehicles or requiring a dangerous goods 
driver licence – refer to definition in Table 3)
A person is not fit to hold an unconditional 
licence:
•	 if the person’s uncorrected visual acuity is 
worse than 6/9 in the better eye; or
•	 if the person’s uncorrected visual acuity is 
worse than 6/18 in either eye.
A conditional licence may be considered 
by the driver licensing authority subject to 
periodic review if the standard is met with 
corrective lenses*.
If the person’s vision is worse than 6/18 in 
the worse eye, a conditional licence may be 
considered by the driver licensing authority 
subject to periodic review, provided the 
visual acuity in the better eye is 6/9 (with or 
without corrective lenses*) according to the 
treating optometrist or ophthalmologist. 
The driver licensing authority will take into 
account:
•	 the nature of the driving task; and
•	 the nature of any underlying disorder; and
•	 any other restriction advised by the 
optometrist or ophthalmologist.
* Refer to section 10.2.7. Orthokeratology 
therapy for information on meeting the 
standard using orthokeratology therapy.

4. AFTD2022-EXP-bbf242d555576d02

Section 1.3 · PDF 70 · Printed page 59 · Original PDF

Commercial standards
(Drivers of heavy vehicles, public passenger 
vehicles or requiring a dangerous goods 
driver licence – refer to definition in Table 3)
A person should not drive for 5 
years following a single blackout of 
undetermined nature.
A person should not drive for 10 years 
following two or more blackouts of 
undetermined nature separated by a 24-
hour period.
A person is not fit to hold an unconditional 
licence:
•	 if the person has experienced blackouts 
that cannot be diagnosed as syncope, 
seizure or another condition.
If there has been a single blackout or more 
than one blackout within a 24-hour period, 
a conditional licence may be considered 
by the driver licensing authority subject to 
at least annual review, taking into account 
information provided by an appropriate 
specialist as to whether the following 
criterion is met:
•	 there have been no further blackouts for 
at least 5 years.
If there have been two or more blackouts 
separated by at least 24 hours, a 
conditional licence may be considered by 
the driver licensing authority subject to at 
least annual review, taking into account 
information provided by an appropriate 
specialist as to whether the following 
criterion is met:
•	 there have been no further blackouts for 
at least 10 years.
5. AFTD2022-EXP-42507db0424f7a27

Section 3.3 · PDF 112 · Printed page 101 · Original PDF

Commercial standards
(Drivers of heavy vehicles, public passenger 
vehicles or requiring a dangerous goods driver 
licence – refer to definition in Table 3)
A person with diabetes treated by diet and 
exercise alone may drive without licence 
restriction. They should he reviewed by their 
treating doctor periodically regarding the 
progression of their diabetes.
A person is not fit to hold an unconditional 
licence:
•	 if the person has non–insulin treated 
diabetes mellitus and is being treated with 
glucose-lowering agents other than insulin.
A conditional licence may be considered 
by the driver licensing authority subject to at 
least annual review, taking into consideration 
the nature of the driving task and information 
provided by an endocrinologist or consultant 
physician specialising in diabetes* on whether 
the following criteria are met:
•	 there is no recent history of a ‘severe 
hypoglycaemic event’ as assessed by the 
specialist; and
•	 the person experiences early warning 
symptoms (awareness) of hypoglycaemia; 
and
•	 the person is following a treatment regimen 
that minimises the risk of hypoglycaemia; 
and
•	 there is an absence of end-organ 
effects that may affect driving as per this 
publication.
* For a commercial driver with type 2 diabetes 
who is being treated with metformin alone, the 
annual review for a conditional licence may 
be undertaken by the driver’s treating doctor 
upon mutual agreement of the treating doctor, 
specialist and driver licensing authority. The 
initial granting of a conditional licence must, 
however, be based on information provided by 
the specialist.

•	 the standard is able to be met with a hearing 
aid***.
If the standard is not able to be met with a hearing 
aid, further individualised assessment should be 
offered. 
A conditional licence may be considered by the 
driver licensing authority subject to periodic review*, 
taking into account:
•	 the nature of the driving task; and
•	 information provided by an ENT specialist or 
audiologist**; and
•	 the results of a practical driver assessment if 
required. 
* Stable conditions may not require periodic review. 
** Refer to section 4.2. General assessment and 
management guidelines.
*** In some cases, noise amplification as a result of 
wearing hearing aids may lead to driver distraction 
and may warrant individualised assessment to 
determine fitness to drive without the hearing aid 
(refer to 4.2. General assessment and management 
guidelines).
4. AFTD2022-EXP-2332d9548f2abd01
Section 1.2.3 · PDF 68 · Printed page 57 · Original PDF
1.2.3. Blackouts due to medical 
causes not covered in the standards
If the cause of the blackout is determined 
to be a medical condition not covered in 
the standards, then first principles regarding 
fitness to drive should be applied (refer to 
Part A section 2. Assessing fitness to drive 
– general guidance). Considerations include 
the likelihood of recurrence of blackout and 
the treatability of the condition as well as the 
nature of the driving task. There should also be 
an appropriate review period. A more stringent 
approach should be considered for commercial 
vehicle drivers.
5. AFTD2022-DM-COM-009
Section 3.3.2 · PDF 110 · Printed page 99 · Original PDF
3.3.2. Recommendation and 
review of conditional licences for 
commercial vehicle drivers
It is a general requirement that conditional 
licences for commercial vehicle drivers are 
issued by the driver licensing authority based on 
advice from an appropriate medical specialist 
(endocrinologist or consultant physician 
specialising in diabetes) and that these drivers 
are reviewed periodically by the specialist to 
determine their ongoing fitness to drive (refer 
to Part A section 4.4. Conditional licences). For 
commercial drivers receiving insulin treatment, at 
least three months of blood glucose monitoring 
records should be reviewed in assessing fitness 
to drive.

1. AFTD2022-EXP-f57fef6c660a1e6d
Section 2.3.1 · PDF 99 · Printed page 88 · Original PDF
Commercial standards
(Drivers of heavy vehicles, public passenger 
vehicles or requiring a dangerous goods 
driver licence – refer to definition in Table 3)
A person is not fit to hold an unconditional 
licence:
•	 if the person has blood pressure 
consistently > 170 systolic or > 100 diastolic 
(treated or untreated).
A conditional licence may be considered 
by the driver licensing authority subject to 
annual review, taking into account the nature 
of the driving task and information provided 
by the treating specialist* as to whether the 
following criteria are met:
•	 the person is treated with antihypertensive 
therapy and effective control of 
hypertension is achieved over a 4-week 
follow-up period; and
•	 there are no side effects from the 
medication that will impair safe driving; and
•	 there is no evidence of damage to target 
organs relevant to driving.
* Ongoing fitness to drive for commercial 
vehicle drivers may be assessed by the 
treating GP provided this is mutually agreed 
by the specialist, GP and driver licensing 
authority. The initial granting of a conditional 
licence must, however, be based on 
information provided by the specialist.
2. AFTD2022-EXP-a09b64ac70a92828
Section 10.3 · PDF 220 · Printed page 209 · Original PDF
Commercial standards
(Drivers of heavy vehicles, public passenger 
vehicles or requiring a dangerous goods 
driver licence – refer to definition in Table 3)
A person is not fit to hold an unconditional 
licence:
•	 if the person’s uncorrected visual acuity is 
worse than 6/9 in the better eye; or
•	 if the person’s uncorrected visual acuity is 
worse than 6/18 in either eye.
A conditional licence may be considered 
by the driver licensing authority subject to 
periodic review if the standard is met with 
corrective lenses*.
If the person’s vision is worse than 6/18 in 
the worse eye, a conditional licence may be 
considered by the driver licensing authority 
subject to periodic review, provided the 
visual acuity in the better eye is 6/9 (with or 
without corrective lenses*) according to the 
treating optometrist or ophthalmologist. 
The driver licensing authority will take into 
account:
•	 the nature of the driving task; and
•	 the nature of any underlying disorder; and
•	 any other restriction advised by the 
optometrist or ophthalmologist.
* Refer to section 10.2.7. Orthokeratology 
therapy for information on meeting the 
standard using orthokeratology therapy.
3. AFTD2022-EXP-7f3c434bba3c53df
Section 4.3 · PDF 120 · Printed page 109 · Original PDF
Commercial standards
(Drivers of heavy vehicles, public passenger vehicles 
or requiring a dangerous goods driver licence – 
refer to definition in Table 3)
Compliance with the standard should be clinically 
assessed initially. If the initial clinical assessment 
indicates possible hearing loss, the person should 
be referred for audiometry.
A person is not fit to hold an unconditional licence:
•	 if the person has unaided hearing loss ≥ 40 dB 
in the better ear (averaged over the frequencies 
0.5, 1, 2 and 3 KHz).
A conditional licence may be considered by the 
driver licensing authority subject to periodic review*, 
taking into account the nature of the driving task 
and information provided by an ENT specialist or 
audiologist**, as to whether:
•	 the standard is able to be met with a hearing 
aid***.
If the standard is not able to be met with a hearing 
aid, further individualised assessment should be 
offered. 
A conditional licence may be considered by the 
driver licensing authority subject to periodic review*, 
taking into account:
•	 the nature of the driving task; and
•	 information provided by an ENT specialist or 
audiologist**; and
•	 the results of a practical driver assessment if 
required. 
* Stable conditions may not require periodic review. 
** Refer to section 4.2. General assessment and 
management guidelines.
*** In some cases, noise amplification as a result of 
wearing hearing aids may lead to driver distraction 
and may warrant individualised assessment to 
determine fitness to drive without the hearing aid 
(refer to 4.2. General assessment and management 
guidelines).
4. AFTD2022-EXP-bbf242d555576d02
Section 1.3 · PDF 70 · Printed page 59 · Original PDF
Commercial standards
(Drivers of heavy vehicles, public passenger 
vehicles or requiring a dangerous goods 
driver licence – refer to definition in Table 3)
A person should not drive for 5 
years following a single blackout of 
undetermined nature.
A person should not drive for 10 years 
following two or more blackouts of 
undetermined nature separated by a 24-
hour period.
A person is not fit to hold an unconditional 
licence:
•	 if the person has experienced blackouts 
that cannot be diagnosed as syncope, 
seizure or another condition.
If there has been a single blackout or more 
than one blackout within a 24-hour period, 
a conditional licence may be considered 
by the driver licensing authority subject to 
at least annual review, taking into account 
information provided by an appropriate 
specialist as to whether the following 
criterion is met:
•	 there have been no further blackouts for 
at least 5 years.
If there have been two or more blackouts 
separated by at least 24 hours, a 
conditional licence may be considered by 
the driver licensing authority subject to at 
least annual review, taking into account 
information provided by an appropriate 
specialist as to whether the following 
criterion is met:
•	 there have been no further blackouts for 
at least 10 years.
5. AFTD2022-EXP-42507db0424f7a27
Section 3.3 · PDF 112 · Printed page 101 · Original PDF
Commercial standards
(Drivers of heavy vehicles, public passenger 
vehicles or requiring a dangerous goods driver 
licence – refer to definition in Table 3)
A person with diabetes treated by diet and 
exercise alone may drive without licence 
restriction. They should he reviewed by their 
treating doctor periodically regarding the 
progression of their diabetes.
A person is not fit to hold an unconditional 
licence:
•	 if the person has non–insulin treated 
diabetes mellitus and is being treated with 
glucose-lowering agents other than insulin.
A conditional licence may be considered 
by the driver licensing authority subject to at 
least annual review, taking into consideration 
the nature of the driving task and information 
provided by an endocrinologist or consultant 
physician specialising in diabetes* on whether 
the following criteria are met:
•	 there is no recent history of a ‘severe 
hypoglycaemic event’ as assessed by the 
specialist; and
•	 the person experiences early warning 
symptoms (awareness) of hypoglycaemia; 
and
•	 the person is following a treatment regimen 
that minimises the risk of hypoglycaemia; 
and
•	 there is an absence of end-organ 
effects that may affect driving as per this 
publication.
* For a commercial driver with type 2 diabetes 
who is being treated with metformin alone, the 
annual review for a conditional licence may 
be undertaken by the driver’s treating doctor 
upon mutual agreement of the treating doctor, 
specialist and driver licensing authority. The 
initial granting of a conditional licence must, 
however, be based on information provided by 
the specialist.

According to guideline AFTD2022-HTN-COM-001, a person is not fit if BP is consistently >170 systolic or >100 diastolic. The patient's values are below these thresholds.\n\n2. **Vision**: Uncorrected visual acuity is 6/6 in both eyes. Guideline AFTD2022-EXP-896156b1ec73be6c requires a better eye of at least 6/9 and a worse eye of at least 6/18 for commercial drivers. The patient exceeds these requirements. No visual field defects, diplopia, or monocular vision were present.\n\n3. **Hearing**: Clinical assessment indicates no hearing loss. Guideline AFTD2022-EXP-7f3c434bba3c53df sets a limit of unaided hearing loss \u226540 dB in the better ear; the absence of loss satisfies this.\n\n4. **Blackout**: No blackout has occurred (verified_patient_facts: blackout.occurred = false). 3. AFTD2022-EXP-7f3c434bba3c53df
Section 4.3 · PDF 120 · Printed page 109 · Original PDF
Commercial standards
(Drivers of heavy vehicles, public passenger vehicles 
or requiring a dangerous goods driver licence – 
refer to definition in Table 3)
Compliance with the standard should be clinically 
assessed initially. If the initial clinical assessment 
indicates possible hearing loss, the person should 
be referred for audiometry.
A person is not fit to hold an unconditional licence:
•	 if the person has unaided hearing loss ≥ 40 dB 
in the better ear (averaged over the frequencies 
0.5, 1, 2 and 3 KHz).
A conditional licence may be considered by the 
driver licensing authority subject to periodic review*, 
taking into account the nature of the driving task 
and information provided by an ENT specialist or 
audiologist**, as to whether:
•	 the standard is able to be met with a hearing 
aid***.
If the standard is not able to be met with a hearing 
aid, further individualised assessment should be 
offered. 
A conditional licence may be considered by the 
driver licensing authority subject to periodic review*, 
taking into account:
•	 the nature of the driving task; and
•	 information provided by an ENT specialist or 
audiologist**; and
•	 the results of a practical driver assessment if 
required. 
* Stable conditions may not require periodic review. 
** Refer to section 4.2. General assessment and 
management guidelines.
*** In some cases, noise amplification as a result of 
wearing hearing aids may lead to driver distraction 
and may warrant individualised assessment to 
determine fitness to drive without the hearing aid 
(refer to 4.2. General assessment and management 
guidelines).
4. AFTD2022-EXP-2332d9548f2abd01
Section 1.2.3 · PDF 68 · Printed page 57 · Original PDF
1.2.3. Blackouts due to medical 
causes not covered in the standards
If the cause of the blackout is determined 
to be a medical condition not covered in 
the standards, then first principles regarding 
fitness to drive should be applied (refer to 
Part A section 2. Assessing fitness to drive 
– general guidance). Considerations include 
the likelihood of recurrence of blackout and 
the treatability of the condition as well as the 
nature of the driving task. There should also be 
an appropriate review period. A more stringent 
approach should be considered for commercial 
vehicle drivers.
5. AFTD2022-DM-COM-009
Section 3.3.2 · PDF 110 · Printed page 99 · Original PDF
3.3.2. Recommendation and 
review of conditional licences for 
commercial vehicle drivers
It is a general requirement that conditional 
licences for commercial vehicle drivers are 
issued by the driver licensing authority based on 
advice from an appropriate medical specialist 
(endocrinologist or consultant physician 
specialising in diabetes) and that these drivers 
are reviewed periodically by the specialist to 
determine their ongoing fitness to drive (refer 
to Part A section 4.4. Conditional licences). For 
commercial drivers receiving insulin treatment, at 
least three months of blood glucose monitoring 
records should be reviewed in assessing fitness 
to drive.

1. AFTD2022-EXP-f57fef6c660a1e6d
Section 2.3.1 · PDF 99 · Printed page 88 · Original PDF
Commercial standards
(Drivers of heavy vehicles, public passenger 
vehicles or requiring a dangerous goods 
driver licence – refer to definition in Table 3)
A person is not fit to hold an unconditional 
licence:
•	 if the person has blood pressure 
consistently > 170 systolic or > 100 diastolic 
(treated or untreated).
A conditional licence may be considered 
by the driver licensing authority subject to 
annual review, taking into account the nature 
of the driving task and information provided 
by the treating specialist* as to whether the 
following criteria are met:
•	 the person is treated with antihypertensive 
therapy and effective control of 
hypertension is achieved over a 4-week 
follow-up period; and
•	 there are no side effects from the 
medication that will impair safe driving; and
•	 there is no evidence of damage to target 
organs relevant to driving.
* Ongoing fitness to drive for commercial 
vehicle drivers may be assessed by the 
treating GP provided this is mutually agreed 
by the specialist, GP and driver licensing 
authority. The initial granting of a conditional 
licence must, however, be based on 
information provided by the specialist.
2. AFTD2022-EXP-a09b64ac70a92828
Section 10.3 · PDF 220 · Printed page 209 · Original PDF
Commercial standards
(Drivers of heavy vehicles, public passenger 
vehicles or requiring a dangerous goods 
driver licence – refer to definition in Table 3)
A person is not fit to hold an unconditional 
licence:
•	 if the person’s uncorrected visual acuity is 
worse than 6/9 in the better eye; or
•	 if the person’s uncorrected visual acuity is 
worse than 6/18 in either eye.
A conditional licence may be considered 
by the driver licensing authority subject to 
periodic review if the standard is met with 
corrective lenses*.
If the person’s vision is worse than 6/18 in 
the worse eye, a conditional licence may be 
considered by the driver licensing authority 
subject to periodic review, provided the 
visual acuity in the better eye is 6/9 (with or 
without corrective lenses*) according to the 
treating optometrist or ophthalmologist. 
The driver licensing authority will take into 
account:
•	 the nature of the driving task; and
•	 the nature of any underlying disorder; and
•	 any other restriction advised by the 
optometrist or ophthalmologist.
* Refer to section 10.2.7. Orthokeratology 
therapy for information on meeting the 
standard using orthokeratology therapy.
3. AFTD2022-EXP-7f3c434bba3c53df

Commercial standards

Compliance with the standard should be clinically

indicates possible hearing loss, the person should

A person is not fit to hold an unconditional licence:
•	 if the person has unaided hearing loss ≥ 40 dB 
in the better ear (averaged over the frequencies 
0.5, 1, 2 and 3 KHz).
A conditional licence may be considered by the 
driver licensing authority subject to periodic review*, 
taking into account the nature of the driving task 
and information provided by an ENT specialist or

•	 the standard is able to be met with a hearing

If the standard is not able to be met with a hearing

*** In some cases, noise amplification as a result of

4. AFTD2022-EXP-bbf242d555576d02
Section 1.3 · PDF 70 · Printed page 59 · Original PDF
Commercial standards
(Drivers of heavy vehicles, public passenger 
vehicles or requiring a dangerous goods 
driver licence – refer to definition in Table 3)
A person should not drive for 5 
years following a single blackout of 
undetermined nature.
A person should not drive for 10 years 
following two or more blackouts of 
undetermined nature separated by a 24-
hour period.
A person is not fit to hold an unconditional 
licence:
•	 if the person has experienced blackouts 
that cannot be diagnosed as syncope, 
seizure or another condition.
If there has been a single blackout or more 
than one blackout within a 24-hour period, 
a conditional licence may be considered 
by the driver licensing authority subject to 
at least annual review, taking into account 
information provided by an appropriate 
specialist as to whether the following 
criterion is met:
•	 there have been no further blackouts for 
at least 5 years.
If there have been two or more blackouts 
separated by at least 24 hours, a 
conditional licence may be considered by 
the driver licensing authority subject to at 
least annual review, taking into account 
information provided by an appropriate 
specialist as to whether the following 
criterion is met:
•	 there have been no further blackouts for 
at least 10 years.
5. AFTD2022-EXP-42507db0424f7a27
Section 3.3 · PDF 112 · Printed page 101 · Original PDF
Commercial standards
(Drivers of heavy vehicles, public passenger 
vehicles or requiring a dangerous goods driver 
licence – refer to definition in Table 3)
A person with diabetes treated by diet and 
exercise alone may drive without licence 
restriction. They should he reviewed by their 
treating doctor periodically regarding the 
progression of their diabetes.
A person is not fit to hold an unconditional 
licence:
•	 if the person has non–insulin treated 
diabetes mellitus and is being treated with 
glucose-lowering agents other than insulin.
A conditional licence may be considered 
by the driver licensing authority subject to at 
least annual review, taking into consideration 
the nature of the driving task and information 
provided by an endocrinologist or consultant 
physician specialising in diabetes* on whether 
the following criteria are met:
•	 there is no recent history of a ‘severe 
hypoglycaemic event’ as assessed by the 
specialist; and
•	 the person experiences early warning 
symptoms (awareness) of hypoglycaemia; 
and
•	 the person is following a treatment regimen 
that minimises the risk of hypoglycaemia; 
and
•	 there is an absence of end-organ 
effects that may affect driving as per this 
publication.
* For a commercial driver with type 2 diabetes 
who is being treated with metformin alone, the 
annual review for a conditional licence may 
be undertaken by the driver’s treating doctor 
upon mutual agreement of the treating doctor, 
specialist and driver licensing authority. The 
initial granting of a conditional licence must, 
however, be based on information provided by 
the specialist.

A person is not fit to hold an unconditional licence:
•	 if the person has unaided hearing loss ≥ 40 dB 
in the better ear (averaged over the frequencies 
0.5, 1, 2 and 3 KHz).
A conditional licence may be considered by the 
driver licensing authority subject to periodic review*, 
taking into account the nature of the driving task 
and information provided by an ENT specialist or 
audiologist**, as to whether:
•	 the standard is able to be met with a hearing 
aid***.
If the standard is not able to be met with a hearing 
aid, further individualised assessment should be 
offered. 
A conditional licence may be considered by the 
driver licensing authority subject to periodic review*, 
taking into account:
•	 the nature of the driving task; and
•	 information provided by an ENT specialist or 
audiologist**; and
•	 the results of a practical driver assessment if 
required. 
* Stable conditions may not require periodic review. 
** Refer to section 4.2. General assessment and 
management guidelines.
*** In some cases, noise amplification as a result of 
wearing hearing aids may lead to driver distraction 
and may warrant individualised assessment to 
determine fitness to drive without the hearing aid 
(refer to 4.2. General assessment and management 
guidelines).
4. AFTD2022-EXP-2332d9548f2abd01
Section 1.2.3 · PDF 68 · Printed page 57 · Original PDF
1.2.3. Blackouts due to medical 
causes not covered in the standards
If the cause of the blackout is determined 
to be a medical condition not covered in 
the standards, then first principles regarding 
fitness to drive should be applied (refer to 
Part A section 2. Assessing fitness to drive 
– general guidance). Considerations include 
the likelihood of recurrence of blackout and 
the treatability of the condition as well as the 
nature of the driving task. There should also be 
an appropriate review period. A more stringent 
approach should be considered for commercial 
vehicle drivers.
5. AFTD2022-DM-COM-009
Section 3.3.2 · PDF 110 · Printed page 99 · Original PDF
3.3.2. Recommendation and 
review of conditional licences for 
commercial vehicle drivers
It is a general requirement that conditional 
licences for commercial vehicle drivers are 
issued by the driver licensing authority based on 
advice from an appropriate medical specialist 
(endocrinologist or consultant physician 
specialising in diabetes) and that these drivers 
are reviewed periodically by the specialist to 
determine their ongoing fitness to drive (refer 
to Part A section 4.4. Conditional licences). For 
commercial drivers receiving insulin treatment, at 
least three months of blood glucose monitoring 
records should be reviewed in assessing fitness 
to drive.

1. AFTD2022-EXP-f57fef6c660a1e6d
Section 2.3.1 · PDF 99 · Printed page 88 · Original PDF
Commercial standards
(Drivers of heavy vehicles, public passenger 
vehicles or requiring a dangerous goods 
driver licence – refer to definition in Table 3)
A person is not fit to hold an unconditional 
licence:
•	 if the person has blood pressure 
consistently > 170 systolic or > 100 diastolic 
(treated or untreated).
A conditional licence may be considered 
by the driver licensing authority subject to 
annual review, taking into account the nature 
of the driving task and information provided 
by the treating specialist* as to whether the 
following criteria are met:
•	 the person is treated with antihypertensive 
therapy and effective control of 
hypertension is achieved over a 4-week 
follow-up period; and
•	 there are no side effects from the 
medication that will impair safe driving; and
•	 there is no evidence of damage to target 
organs relevant to driving.
* Ongoing fitness to drive for commercial 
vehicle drivers may be assessed by the 
treating GP provided this is mutually agreed 
by the specialist, GP and driver licensing 
authority. The initial granting of a conditional 
licence must, however, be based on 
information provided by the specialist.
2. AFTD2022-EXP-a09b64ac70a92828
Section 10.3 · PDF 220 · Printed page 209 · Original PDF
Commercial standards
(Drivers of heavy vehicles, public passenger 
vehicles or requiring a dangerous goods 
driver licence – refer to definition in Table 3)
A person is not fit to hold an unconditional 
licence:
•	 if the person’s uncorrected visual acuity is 
worse than 6/9 in the better eye; or
•	 if the person’s uncorrected visual acuity is 
worse than 6/18 in either eye.
A conditional licence may be considered 
by the driver licensing authority subject to 
periodic review if the standard is met with 
corrective lenses*.
If the person’s vision is worse than 6/18 in 
the worse eye, a conditional licence may be 
considered by the driver licensing authority 
subject to periodic review, provided the 
visual acuity in the better eye is 6/9 (with or 
without corrective lenses*) according to the 
treating optometrist or ophthalmologist. 
The driver licensing authority will take into 
account:
•	 the nature of the driving task; and
•	 the nature of any underlying disorder; and
•	 any other restriction advised by the 
optometrist or ophthalmologist.
* Refer to section 10.2.7. Orthokeratology 
therapy for information on meeting the 
standard using orthokeratology therapy.

in the better ear (averaged over the frequencies 
0.5, 1, 2 and 3 KHz).
A conditional licence may be considered by the 
driver licensing authority subject to periodic review*,

and information provided by an ENT specialist or

audiologist**; and

* Stable conditions may not require periodic review. 
** Refer to section 4.2. General assessment and

*** In some cases, noise amplification as a result of 
wearing hearing aids may lead to driver distraction

4. AFTD2022-EXP-bbf242d555576d02
Section 1.3 · PDF 70 · Printed page 59 · Original PDF
Commercial standards
(Drivers of heavy vehicles, public passenger 
vehicles or requiring a dangerous goods 
driver licence – refer to definition in Table 3)
A person should not drive for 5 
years following a single blackout of 
undetermined nature.
A person should not drive for 10 years 
following two or more blackouts of 
undetermined nature separated by a 24-
hour period.
A person is not fit to hold an unconditional 
licence:
•	 if the person has experienced blackouts 
that cannot be diagnosed as syncope, 
seizure or another condition.
If there has been a single blackout or more 
than one blackout within a 24-hour period, 
a conditional licence may be considered 
by the driver licensing authority subject to 
at least annual review, taking into account 
information provided by an appropriate 
specialist as to whether the following 
criterion is met:
•	 there have been no further blackouts for 
at least 5 years.
If there have been two or more blackouts 
separated by at least 24 hours, a 
conditional licence may be considered by 
the driver licensing authority subject to at 
least annual review, taking into account 
information provided by an appropriate 
specialist as to whether the following 
criterion is met:
•	 there have been no further blackouts for 
at least 10 years.
5. AFTD2022-EXP-42507db0424f7a27
Section 3.3 · PDF 112 · Printed page 101 · Original PDF
Commercial standards
(Drivers of heavy vehicles, public passenger 
vehicles or requiring a dangerous goods driver 
licence – refer to definition in Table 3)
A person with diabetes treated by diet and 
exercise alone may drive without licence 
restriction. They should he reviewed by their 
treating doctor periodically regarding the 
progression of their diabetes.
A person is not fit to hold an unconditional 
licence:
•	 if the person has non–insulin treated 
diabetes mellitus and is being treated with 
glucose-lowering agents other than insulin.
A conditional licence may be considered 
by the driver licensing authority subject to at 
least annual review, taking into consideration 
the nature of the driving task and information 
provided by an endocrinologist or consultant 
physician specialising in diabetes* on whether 
the following criteria are met:
•	 there is no recent history of a ‘severe 
hypoglycaemic event’ as assessed by the 
specialist; and
•	 the person experiences early warning 
symptoms (awareness) of hypoglycaemia; 
and
•	 the person is following a treatment regimen 
that minimises the risk of hypoglycaemia; 
and
•	 there is an absence of end-organ 
effects that may affect driving as per this 
publication.
* For a commercial driver with type 2 diabetes 
who is being treated with metformin alone, the 
annual review for a conditional licence may 
be undertaken by the driver’s treating doctor 
upon mutual agreement of the treating doctor, 
specialist and driver licensing authority. The 
initial granting of a conditional licence must, 
however, be based on information provided by 
the specialist.

Commercial standards
(Drivers of heavy vehicles, public passenger 
vehicles or requiring a dangerous goods 
driver licence – refer to definition in Table 3)
A person should not drive for 5 
years following a single blackout of 
undetermined nature.
A person should not drive for 10 years 
following two or more blackouts of 
undetermined nature separated by a 24-
hour period.
A person is not fit to hold an unconditional 
licence:
•	 if the person has experienced blackouts 
that cannot be diagnosed as syncope, 
seizure or another condition.
If there has been a single blackout or more 
than one blackout within a 24-hour period, 
a conditional licence may be considered 
by the driver licensing authority subject to 
at least annual review, taking into account 
information provided by an appropriate 
specialist as to whether the following 
criterion is met:
•	 there have been no further blackouts for 
at least 5 years.
If there have been two or more blackouts 
separated by at least 24 hours, a 
conditional licence may be considered by 
the driver licensing authority subject to at 
least annual review, taking into account 
information provided by an appropriate 
specialist as to whether the following 
criterion is met:
•	 there have been no further blackouts for 
at least 10 years.
5. AFTD2022-EXP-42507db0424f7a27
Section 3.3 · PDF 112 · Printed page 101 · Original PDF
Commercial standards
(Drivers of heavy vehicles, public passenger 
vehicles or requiring a dangerous goods driver 
licence – refer to definition in Table 3)
A person with diabetes treated by diet and 
exercise alone may drive without licence 
restriction. They should he reviewed by their 
treating doctor periodically regarding the 
progression of their diabetes.
A person is not fit to hold an unconditional 
licence:
•	 if the person has non–insulin treated 
diabetes mellitus and is being treated with 
glucose-lowering agents other than insulin.
A conditional licence may be considered 
by the driver licensing authority subject to at 
least annual review, taking into consideration 
the nature of the driving task and information 
provided by an endocrinologist or consultant 
physician specialising in diabetes* on whether 
the following criteria are met:
•	 there is no recent history of a ‘severe 
hypoglycaemic event’ as assessed by the 
specialist; and
•	 the person experiences early warning 
symptoms (awareness) of hypoglycaemia; 
and
•	 the person is following a treatment regimen 
that minimises the risk of hypoglycaemia; 
and
•	 there is an absence of end-organ 
effects that may affect driving as per this 
publication.
* For a commercial driver with type 2 diabetes 
who is being treated with metformin alone, the 
annual review for a conditional licence may 
be undertaken by the driver’s treating doctor 
upon mutual agreement of the treating doctor, 
specialist and driver licensing authority. The 
initial granting of a conditional licence must, 
however, be based on information provided by 
the specialist.

1. AFTD2022-HTN-COM-001
Section 2.3.1 · PDF 99 · Printed page 88 · Original PDF
A person is not fit to hold an unconditional 
licence:
•	 if the person has blood pressure 
consistently > 170 systolic or > 100 diastolic 
(treated or untreated).
2. AFTD2022-EXP-7de596b87146a1f5
Section 2.2.3 · PDF 77 · Printed page 66 · Original PDF
2.2.3. High blood pressure
The cut-off blood pressure values at which 
a person is considered unfit to hold an 
unconditional licence do not reflect usual goals 
for managing hypertension. Rather, they reflect 
levels that are likely to be associated with 
sudden incapacity due to neurological events 
(e.g. stroke). The cut-off points are based on 
expert opinion.
It is a general requirement that conditional 
licences for commercial vehicle drivers are 
issued by the driver licensing authority based 
on the advice of an appropriate medical 
specialist and that these drivers are reviewed 
periodically by the specialist to determine 
their ongoing fitness to drive (refer to Part A 
section 4.4. Conditional licences). In the case 
of high blood pressure, ongoing fitness to 
drive may be assessed by the treating general 
practitioner, provided this is mutually agreed by 
the specialist and the general practitioner. The 
initial recommendation of a conditional licence 
must, however, be based on the opinion of 
the specialist.
3. AFTD2022-EXP-f57fef6c660a1e6d
Section 2.3.1 · PDF 99 · Printed page 88 · Original PDF
Commercial standards
(Drivers of heavy vehicles, public passenger 
vehicles or requiring a dangerous goods 
driver licence – refer to definition in Table 3)
A person is not fit to hold an unconditional 
licence:
•	 if the person has blood pressure 
consistently > 170 systolic or > 100 diastolic 
(treated or untreated).
A conditional licence may be considered 
by the driver licensing authority subject to 
annual review, taking into account the nature 
of the driving task and information provided 
by the treating specialist* as to whether the 
following criteria are met:
•	 the person is treated with antihypertensive 
therapy and effective control of 
hypertension is achieved over a 4-week 
follow-up period; and
•	 there are no side effects from the 
medication that will impair safe driving; and
•	 there is no evidence of damage to target 
organs relevant to driving.
* Ongoing fitness to drive for commercial 
vehicle drivers may be assessed by the 
treating GP provided this is mutually agreed 
by the specialist, GP and driver licensing 
authority. The initial granting of a conditional 
licence must, however, be based on 
information provided by the specialist.

1. AFTD2022-HTN-COM-001
Section 2.3.1 · PDF 99 · Printed page 88 · Original PDF
A person is not fit to hold an unconditional 
licence:
•	 if the person has blood pressure 
consistently > 170 systolic or > 100 diastolic 
(treated or untreated).
2. AFTD2022-EXP-7de596b87146a1f5
Section 2.2.3 · PDF 77 · Printed page 66 · Original PDF
2.2.3. High blood pressure
The cut-off blood pressure values at which 
a person is considered unfit to hold an 
unconditional licence do not reflect usual goals 
for managing hypertension. Rather, they reflect 
levels that are likely to be associated with 
sudden incapacity due to neurological events 
(e.g. stroke). The cut-off points are based on 
expert opinion.
It is a general requirement that conditional 
licences for commercial vehicle drivers are 
issued by the driver licensing authority based 
on the advice of an appropriate medical 
specialist and that these drivers are reviewed 
periodically by the specialist to determine 
their ongoing fitness to drive (refer to Part A 
section 4.4. Conditional licences). In the case 
of high blood pressure, ongoing fitness to 
drive may be assessed by the treating general 
practitioner, provided this is mutually agreed by 
the specialist and the general practitioner. The 
initial recommendation of a conditional licence 
must, however, be based on the opinion of 
the specialist.
3. AFTD2022-EXP-f57fef6c660a1e6d
Section 2.3.1 · PDF 99 · Printed page 88 · Original PDF
Commercial standards
(Drivers of heavy vehicles, public passenger 
vehicles or requiring a dangerous goods 
driver licence – refer to definition in Table 3)
A person is not fit to hold an unconditional 
licence:
•	 if the person has blood pressure 
consistently > 170 systolic or > 100 diastolic 
(treated or untreated).
A conditional licence may be considered 
by the driver licensing authority subject to 
annual review, taking into account the nature 
of the driving task and information provided 
by the treating specialist* as to whether the 
following criteria are met:
•	 the person is treated with antihypertensive 
therapy and effective control of 
hypertension is achieved over a 4-week 
follow-up period; and
•	 there are no side effects from the 
medication that will impair safe driving; and
•	 there is no evidence of damage to target 
organs relevant to driving.
* Ongoing fitness to drive for commercial 
vehicle drivers may be assessed by the 
treating GP provided this is mutually agreed 
by the specialist, GP and driver licensing 
authority. The initial granting of a conditional 
licence must, however, be based on 
information provided by the specialist.

{
  "assessment_outcome": "insufficient_information",
  "explanation": "The patient's blood pressure is consistently recorded at 171/100 mmHg. According to guideline evidence (AFTD2022-HTN-COM-001, AFTD2022-HTN-COM-002), this exceeds the threshold (>170 systolic or >100 diastolic) for holding an unconditional licence. However, a conditional licence requires specific criteria: treatment with antihypertensive therapy, effective control over a 4-week follow-up period, absence of driving-impairing side effects, and no evidence of target organ damage. The nurse note states that 'conditional follow-up is not documented' and provides no data on medication status, treatment efficacy, or target organ health. Therefore, the established restrictive criterion (unfitness for unconditional licence) cannot be overridden by a conditional qualification due to missing verification of required conditions.",

  ],

1. AFTD2022-HTN-COM-001
Section 2.3.1 · PDF 99 · Printed page 88 · Original PDF
A person is not fit to hold an unconditional 
licence:
•	 if the person has blood pressure 
consistently > 170 systolic or > 100 diastolic 
(treated or untreated).
2. AFTD2022-EXP-7de596b87146a1f5
Section 2.2.3 · PDF 77 · Printed page 66 · Original PDF
2.2.3. High blood pressure
The cut-off blood pressure values at which 
a person is considered unfit to hold an 
unconditional licence do not reflect usual goals 
for managing hypertension. Rather, they reflect 
levels that are likely to be associated with 
sudden incapacity due to neurological events 
(e.g. stroke). The cut-off points are based on 
expert opinion.
It is a general requirement that conditional 
licences for commercial vehicle drivers are 
issued by the driver licensing authority based 
on the advice of an appropriate medical 
specialist and that these drivers are reviewed 
periodically by the specialist to determine 
their ongoing fitness to drive (refer to Part A 
section 4.4. Conditional licences). In the case 
of high blood pressure, ongoing fitness to 
drive may be assessed by the treating general 
practitioner, provided this is mutually agreed by 
the specialist and the general practitioner. The 
initial recommendation of a conditional licence 
must, however, be based on the opinion of 
the specialist.
3. AFTD2022-EXP-f57fef6c660a1e6d
Section 2.3.1 · PDF 99 · Printed page 88 · Original PDF
Commercial standards
(Drivers of heavy vehicles, public passenger 
vehicles or requiring a dangerous goods 
driver licence – refer to definition in Table 3)
A person is not fit to hold an unconditional 
licence:
•	 if the person has blood pressure 
consistently > 170 systolic or > 100 diastolic 
(treated or untreated).
A conditional licence may be considered 
by the driver licensing authority subject to 
annual review, taking into account the nature 
of the driving task and information provided 
by the treating specialist* as to whether the 
following criteria are met:
•	 the person is treated with antihypertensive 
therapy and effective control of 
hypertension is achieved over a 4-week 
follow-up period; and
•	 there are no side effects from the 
medication that will impair safe driving; and
•	 there is no evidence of damage to target 
organs relevant to driving.
* Ongoing fitness to drive for commercial 
vehicle drivers may be assessed by the 
treating GP provided this is mutually agreed 
by the specialist, GP and driver licensing 
authority. The initial granting of a conditional 
licence must, however, be based on 
information provided by the specialist.
4. AFTD2022-HTN-COM-002
Section 2.3.1 · PDF 99 · Printed page 88 · Original PDF
A conditional licence may be considered 
by the driver licensing authority subject to 
annual review, taking into account the nature 
of the driving task and information provided 
by the treating specialist* as to whether the 
following criteria are met:
•	 the person is treated with antihypertensive 
therapy and effective control of 
hypertension is achieved over a 4-week 
follow-up period; and
•	 there are no side effects from the 
medication that will impair safe driving; and
•	 there is no evidence of damage to target 
organs relevant to driving.
* Ongoing fitness to drive for commercial 
vehicle drivers may be assessed by the 
treating GP provided this is mutually agreed 
by the specialist, GP and driver licensing 
authority. The initial granting of a conditional 
licence must, however, be based on 
information provided by the specialist.

1. AFTD2022-EXP-3a8e08652c83a2d0
Section 1.2.4 · PDF 69 · Printed page 58 · Original PDF
1.2.4. Blackouts of undetermined 
mechanism
If, despite extensive investigation, the 
mechanism of a blackout cannot be determined, 
fitness to drive should be assessed according 
to section 1.3. Medical standards for licensing. 
The standards for blackout of undetermined 
mechanism are similar to those for seizure.
2. AFTD2022-EXP-2332d9548f2abd01
Section 1.2.3 · PDF 68 · Printed page 57 · Original PDF
1.2.3. Blackouts due to medical 
causes not covered in the standards
If the cause of the blackout is determined 
to be a medical condition not covered in 
the standards, then first principles regarding 
fitness to drive should be applied (refer to 
Part A section 2. Assessing fitness to drive 
– general guidance). Considerations include 
the likelihood of recurrence of blackout and 
the treatability of the condition as well as the 
nature of the driving task. There should also be 
an appropriate review period. A more stringent 
approach should be considered for commercial 
vehicle drivers.
3. AFTD2022-EXP-05643c50d6cf5973
Section 1.2.1 · PDF 68 · Printed page 57 · Original PDF
cardiovascular and neurological investigations 
and referral to several specialists. People should 
be advised not to drive until the mechanism is 
ascertained and the corresponding standard met.
Some drivers may attribute a crash or driving 
mishap to a ‘blackout’ to excuse an event 
that occurred for some other reason such as 
inattention or distraction (e.g. a mobile phone 
conversation). There will also be a small 
proportion of cases in which a clear cause 
cannot be established.
4. AFTD2022-BLK-COM-006
Section 1.3 · PDF 69 · Printed page 58 · Original PDF
themselves with the information in this chapter 
and the tabulated standards before assessing a 
person’s fitness to drive. 
Where a firm diagnosis has been made, the 
standard appropriate to the condition should 
be referred to in this publication (refer to Figure 
6. Management of blackouts and driving). For 
blackouts due to medical causes not covered 
in the standard, refer to first principles (refer to 
Part A section 2. Assessing fitness to drive – 
general guidance). For blackouts where, after 
investigation, it is not possible to diagnose one 
of the conditions covered elsewhere in this 
publication, refer to the table for blackouts of 
uncertain nature over the page.
5. AFTD2022-EXP-5546204ae4ffe0ee
Section 1.3 · PDF 71 · Printed page 60 · Original PDF
Commercial standards
(Drivers of heavy vehicles, public passenger 
vehicles or requiring a dangerous goods 
driver licence – refer to definition in Table 3)
Where a person with one or more blackouts 
of undetermined mechanism does not 
meet the standards above for a conditional 
licence but may, in the opinion of the 
treating specialist, be safe to drive, a 
conditional licence may be considered by 
the driver licensing authority, subject to at 
least annual review:
•	 if the driver licensing authority, after 
considering information provided by the 
treating specialist(s), considers that the 
risk of a crash caused by a blackout is 
acceptably low.

1. AFTD2022-EXP-bbf242d555576d02
Section 1.3 · PDF 70 · Printed page 59 · Original PDF
Commercial standards
(Drivers of heavy vehicles, public passenger 
vehicles or requiring a dangerous goods 
driver licence – refer to definition in Table 3)
A person should not drive for 5 
years following a single blackout of 
undetermined nature.
A person should not drive for 10 years 
following two or more blackouts of 
undetermined nature separated by a 24-
hour period.
A person is not fit to hold an unconditional 
licence:
•	 if the person has experienced blackouts 
that cannot be diagnosed as syncope, 
seizure or another condition.
If there has been a single blackout or more 
than one blackout within a 24-hour period, 
a conditional licence may be considered 
by the driver licensing authority subject to 
at least annual review, taking into account 
information provided by an appropriate 
specialist as to whether the following 
criterion is met:
•	 there have been no further blackouts for 
at least 5 years.
If there have been two or more blackouts 
separated by at least 24 hours, a 
conditional licence may be considered by 
the driver licensing authority subject to at 
least annual review, taking into account 
information provided by an appropriate 
specialist as to whether the following 
criterion is met:
•	 there have been no further blackouts for 
at least 10 years.

1. AFTD2022-EXP-3a8e08652c83a2d0
Section 1.2.4 · PDF 69 · Printed page 58 · Original PDF
1.2.4. Blackouts of undetermined 
mechanism
If, despite extensive investigation, the 
mechanism of a blackout cannot be determined, 
fitness to drive should be assessed according 
to section 1.3. Medical standards for licensing. 
The standards for blackout of undetermined 
mechanism are similar to those for seizure.
2. AFTD2022-EXP-2332d9548f2abd01
Section 1.2.3 · PDF 68 · Printed page 57 · Original PDF
1.2.3. Blackouts due to medical 
causes not covered in the standards
If the cause of the blackout is determined 
to be a medical condition not covered in 
the standards, then first principles regarding 
fitness to drive should be applied (refer to 
Part A section 2. Assessing fitness to drive 
– general guidance). Considerations include 
the likelihood of recurrence of blackout and 
the treatability of the condition as well as the 
nature of the driving task. There should also be 
an appropriate review period. A more stringent 
approach should be considered for commercial 
vehicle drivers.
3. AFTD2022-EXP-05643c50d6cf5973
Section 1.2.1 · PDF 68 · Printed page 57 · Original PDF
cardiovascular and neurological investigations 
and referral to several specialists. People should 
be advised not to drive until the mechanism is 
ascertained and the corresponding standard met.
Some drivers may attribute a crash or driving 
mishap to a ‘blackout’ to excuse an event 
that occurred for some other reason such as 
inattention or distraction (e.g. a mobile phone 
conversation). There will also be a small 
proportion of cases in which a clear cause 
cannot be established.
4. AFTD2022-BLK-COM-006
Section 1.3 · PDF 69 · Printed page 58 · Original PDF
themselves with the information in this chapter 
and the tabulated standards before assessing a 
person’s fitness to drive. 
Where a firm diagnosis has been made, the 
standard appropriate to the condition should 
be referred to in this publication (refer to Figure 
6. Management of blackouts and driving). For 
blackouts due to medical causes not covered 
in the standard, refer to first principles (refer to

5. AFTD2022-EXP-5546204ae4ffe0ee
Section 1.3 · PDF 71 · Printed page 60 · Original PDF
Commercial standards
(Drivers of heavy vehicles, public passenger 
vehicles or requiring a dangerous goods 
driver licence – refer to definition in Table 3)
Where a person with one or more blackouts 
of undetermined mechanism does not 
meet the standards above for a conditional 
licence but may, in the opinion of the 
treating specialist, be safe to drive, a 
conditional licence may be considered by 
the driver licensing authority, subject to at 
least annual review:
•	 if the driver licensing authority, after 
considering information provided by the 
treating specialist(s), considers that the 
risk of a crash caused by a blackout is 
acceptably low.

1. AFTD2022-EXP-bbf242d555576d02
Section 1.3 · PDF 70 · Printed page 59 · Original PDF
Commercial standards
(Drivers of heavy vehicles, public passenger 
vehicles or requiring a dangerous goods 
driver licence – refer to definition in Table 3)
A person should not drive for 5 
years following a single blackout of 
undetermined nature.
A person should not drive for 10 years 
following two or more blackouts of 
undetermined nature separated by a 24-
hour period.
A person is not fit to hold an unconditional 
licence:
•	 if the person has experienced blackouts 
that cannot be diagnosed as syncope, 
seizure or another condition.
If there has been a single blackout or more 
than one blackout within a 24-hour period, 
a conditional licence may be considered 
by the driver licensing authority subject to 
at least annual review, taking into account 
information provided by an appropriate 
specialist as to whether the following 
criterion is met:
•	 there have been no further blackouts for 
at least 5 years.
If there have been two or more blackouts 
separated by at least 24 hours, a 
conditional licence may be considered by 
the driver licensing authority subject to at 
least annual review, taking into account 
information provided by an appropriate 
specialist as to whether the following 
criterion is met:
•	 there have been no further blackouts for 
at least 10 years.

{
  "assessment_outcome": "insufficient_information",
  "explanation": "The patient has a confirmed history of blackout (verified_patient_facts: blackout.occurred = true) with the mechanism status explicitly recorded as 'under_investigation' (verified_patient_facts: blackout.mechanism_status). According to guideline evidence AFTD2022-EXP-3a8e08652c83a2d0, blackouts of undetermined mechanism require assessment according to section 1.3 standards, which are similar to seizure standards. Guideline AFTD2022-BLK-COM-006 further states that where a firm diagnosis has not been made, the appropriate standard should be referred to, and for commercial drivers, a conditional licence is only considered if the risk of a crash caused by a blackout is acceptably low after specialist review. Since the mechanism remains undetermined and no specific medical condition (e.g., seizure, cardiac arrhythmia) has been diagnosed or treated, it is not possible to establish whether established restrictive criteria for a conditional licence are met. The nurse_note confirms the investigation is ongoing but does not provide verified facts establishing fitness; therefore, under the rule that missing information is not normal and no guideline evidence can establish fitness without a diagnosis, the assessment cannot conclude that the driver meets licensing standards.",
  "source_ids": [
    "AFTD2022-EXP-3a8e08652c83a2d0",
    "AFTD2022-BLK-COM-006"
  ],
  "fact_fields": [
    "blackout.occurred",
    "blackout.mechanism_status"
  ]
}
1. AFTD2022-EXP-3a8e08652c83a2d0
Section 1.2.4 · PDF 69 · Printed page 58 · Original PDF
1.2.4. Blackouts of undetermined 
mechanism
If, despite extensive investigation, the 
mechanism of a blackout cannot be determined, 
fitness to drive should be assessed according 
to section 1.3. Medical standards for licensing. 
The standards for blackout of undetermined 
mechanism are similar to those for seizure.
2. AFTD2022-EXP-2332d9548f2abd01
Section 1.2.3 · PDF 68 · Printed page 57 · Original PDF
1.2.3. Blackouts due to medical 
causes not covered in the standards
If the cause of the blackout is determined 
to be a medical condition not covered in 
the standards, then first principles regarding 
fitness to drive should be applied (refer to 
Part A section 2. Assessing fitness to drive 
– general guidance). Considerations include 
the likelihood of recurrence of blackout and 
the treatability of the condition as well as the 
nature of the driving task. There should also be 
an appropriate review period. A more stringent 
approach should be considered for commercial 
vehicle drivers.
3. AFTD2022-EXP-05643c50d6cf5973
Section 1.2.1 · PDF 68 · Printed page 57 · Original PDF
cardiovascular and neurological investigations 
and referral to several specialists. People should 
be advised not to drive until the mechanism is 
ascertained and the corresponding standard met.
Some drivers may attribute a crash or driving 
mishap to a ‘blackout’ to excuse an event 
that occurred for some other reason such as 
inattention or distraction (e.g. a mobile phone 
conversation). There will also be a small 
proportion of cases in which a clear cause 
cannot be established.
4. AFTD2022-BLK-COM-006
Section 1.3 · PDF 69 · Printed page 58 · Original PDF

5. AFTD2022-EXP-5546204ae4ffe0ee
Section 1.3 · PDF 71 · Printed page 60 · Original PDF
Commercial standards
(Drivers of heavy vehicles, public passenger 
vehicles or requiring a dangerous goods 
driver licence – refer to definition in Table 3)
Where a person with one or more blackouts 
of undetermined mechanism does not 
meet the standards above for a conditional 
licence but may, in the opinion of the 
treating specialist, be safe to drive, a 
conditional licence may be considered by 
the driver licensing authority, subject to at 
least annual review:
•	 if the driver licensing authority, after 
considering information provided by the 
treating specialist(s), considers that the 
risk of a crash caused by a blackout is 
acceptably low.

However, the mechanism of this blackout is currently 'under_investigation' (verified_patient_facts: blackout.mechanism_status = 'under_investigation'). According to guideline evidence AFTD2022-EXP-bbf242d55576d02 and AFTD2022-EXP-3a8e08652c83a2d0, fitness for commercial driving cannot be determined until the mechanism is ascertained. If the cause remains undetermined, standards for blackouts of undetermined nature apply (Section 1.3), which require a period of no further blackouts (5 or 10 years) and specialist review before any conditional licence consideration. Since the investigation is ongoing, it is not established whether the blackout was syncope, seizure, or another condition, nor has the required observation period elapsed. Therefore, no definitive assessment outcome regarding fitness can be established at this time.",

1. AFTD2022-EXP-bbf242d555576d02
Section 1.3 · PDF 70 · Printed page 59 · Original PDF
Commercial standards
(Drivers of heavy vehicles, public passenger 
vehicles or requiring a dangerous goods 
driver licence – refer to definition in Table 3)
A person should not drive for 5 
years following a single blackout of 
undetermined nature.
A person should not drive for 10 years 
following two or more blackouts of 
undetermined nature separated by a 24-
hour period.
A person is not fit to hold an unconditional 
licence:
•	 if the person has experienced blackouts 
that cannot be diagnosed as syncope, 
seizure or another condition.
If there has been a single blackout or more 
than one blackout within a 24-hour period, 
a conditional licence may be considered 
by the driver licensing authority subject to 
at least annual review, taking into account 
information provided by an appropriate 
specialist as to whether the following 
criterion is met:
•	 there have been no further blackouts for 
at least 5 years.
If there have been two or more blackouts 
separated by at least 24 hours, a 
conditional licence may be considered by 
the driver licensing authority subject to at 
least annual review, taking into account 
information provided by an appropriate 
specialist as to whether the following 
criterion is met:
•	 there have been no further blackouts for 
at least 10 years.

1. AFTD2022-EXP-3a8e08652c83a2d0
Section 1.2.4 · PDF 69 · Printed page 58 · Original PDF
1.2.4. Blackouts of undetermined 
mechanism
If, despite extensive investigation, the 
mechanism of a blackout cannot be determined, 
fitness to drive should be assessed according 
to section 1.3. Medical standards for licensing. 
The standards for blackout of undetermined 
mechanism are similar to those for seizure.
2. AFTD2022-BLK-COM-004
Section 1.3 · PDF 70 · Printed page 59 · Original PDF
A person should not drive for 5 
years following a single blackout of 
undetermined nature.
A person should not drive for 10 years 
following two or more blackouts of 
undetermined nature separated by a 24-
hour period.
A person is not fit to hold an unconditional 
licence:
•	 if the person has experienced blackouts 
that cannot be diagnosed as syncope, 
seizure or another condition.
If there has been a single blackout or more 
than one blackout within a 24-hour period, 
a conditional licence may be considered 
by the driver licensing authority subject to 
at least annual review, taking into account 
information provided by an appropriate 
specialist as to whether the following 
criterion is met:
•	 there have been no further blackouts for 
at least 5 years.
3. AFTD2022-EXP-bbf242d555576d02
Section 1.3 · PDF 70 · Printed page 59 · Original PDF
Commercial standards
(Drivers of heavy vehicles, public passenger 
vehicles or requiring a dangerous goods 
driver licence – refer to definition in Table 3)
A person should not drive for 5 
years following a single blackout of 
undetermined nature.
A person should not drive for 10 years 
following two or more blackouts of 
undetermined nature separated by a 24-
hour period.
A person is not fit to hold an unconditional 
licence:
•	 if the person has experienced blackouts 
that cannot be diagnosed as syncope, 
seizure or another condition.
If there has been a single blackout or more 
than one blackout within a 24-hour period, 
a conditional licence may be considered 
by the driver licensing authority subject to 
at least annual review, taking into account 
information provided by an appropriate 
specialist as to whether the following 
criterion is met:
•	 there have been no further blackouts for 
at least 5 years.
If there have been two or more blackouts 
separated by at least 24 hours, a 
conditional licence may be considered by 
the driver licensing authority subject to at 
least annual review, taking into account 
information provided by an appropriate 
specialist as to whether the following 
criterion is met:
•	 there have been no further blackouts for 
at least 10 years.
4. AFTD2022-EXP-2332d9548f2abd01
Section 1.2.3 · PDF 68 · Printed page 57 · Original PDF
1.2.3. Blackouts due to medical 
causes not covered in the standards
If the cause of the blackout is determined 
to be a medical condition not covered in 
the standards, then first principles regarding 
fitness to drive should be applied (refer to 
Part A section 2. Assessing fitness to drive 
– general guidance). Considerations include 
the likelihood of recurrence of blackout and 
the treatability of the condition as well as the 
nature of the driving task. There should also be 
an appropriate review period. A more stringent 
approach should be considered for commercial 
vehicle drivers.

themselves with the information in this chapter

5. AFTD2022-EXP-5546204ae4ffe0ee
Section 1.3 · PDF 71 · Printed page 60 · Original PDF
Commercial standards
(Drivers of heavy vehicles, public passenger 
vehicles or requiring a dangerous goods 
driver licence – refer to definition in Table 3)
Where a person with one or more blackouts 
of undetermined mechanism does not 
meet the standards above for a conditional 
licence but may, in the opinion of the 
treating specialist, be safe to drive, a 
conditional licence may be considered by 
the driver licensing authority, subject to at 
least annual review:
•	 if the driver licensing authority, after 
considering information provided by the 
treating specialist(s), considers that the 
risk of a crash caused by a blackout is 
acceptably low.

(Drivers of heavy vehicles, public passenger 
vehicles or requiring a dangerous goods 
driver licence – refer to definition in Table 3)
A person should not drive for 5 
years following a single blackout of 
undetermined nature.
A person should not drive for 10 years 
following two or more blackouts of 
undetermined nature separated by a 24-
hour period.
A person is not fit to hold an unconditional 
licence:
•	 if the person has experienced blackouts 
that cannot be diagnosed as syncope, 
seizure or another condition.
If there has been a single blackout or more 
than one blackout within a 24-hour period, 
a conditional licence may be considered 
by the driver licensing authority subject to 
at least annual review, taking into account 
information provided by an appropriate 
specialist as to whether the following 
criterion is met:
•	 there have been no further blackouts for 
at least 5 years.
If there have been two or more blackouts 
separated by at least 24 hours, a 
conditional licence may be considered by 
the driver licensing authority subject to at 
least annual review, taking into account 
information provided by an appropriate 
specialist as to whether the following 
criterion is met:
•	 there have been no further blackouts for 
at least 10 years.
2. AFTD2022-EXP-3a8e08652c83a2d0
Section 1.2.4 · PDF 69 · Printed page 58 · Original PDF
1.2.4. Blackouts of undetermined 
mechanism
If, despite extensive investigation, the 
mechanism of a blackout cannot be determined, 
fitness to drive should be assessed according 
to section 1.3. Medical standards for licensing. 
The standards for blackout of undetermined 
mechanism are similar to those for seizure.
3. AFTD2022-EXP-2332d9548f2abd01
Section 1.2.3 · PDF 68 · Printed page 57 · Original PDF
1.2.3. Blackouts due to medical 
causes not covered in the standards
If the cause of the blackout is determined 
to be a medical condition not covered in 
the standards, then first principles regarding 
fitness to drive should be applied (refer to 
Part A section 2. Assessing fitness to drive 
– general guidance). Considerations include 
the likelihood of recurrence of blackout and 
the treatability of the condition as well as the 
nature of the driving task. There should also be 
an appropriate review period. A more stringent 
approach should be considered for commercial 
vehicle drivers.

themselves with the information in this chapter

5. AFTD2022-EXP-5546204ae4ffe0ee

Commercial standards
(Drivers of heavy vehicles, public passenger 
vehicles or requiring a dangerous goods 
driver licence – refer to definition in Table 3)
Where a person with one or more blackouts 
of undetermined mechanism does not 
meet the standards above for a conditional 
licence but may, in the opinion of the 
treating specialist, be safe to drive, a 
conditional licence may be considered by 
the driver licensing authority, subject to at 
least annual review:
•	 if the driver licensing authority, after 
considering information provided by the 
treating specialist(s), considers that the 
risk of a crash caused by a blackout is 
acceptably low.

information provided by an appropriate 
specialist as to whether the following 
criterion is met:

at least 5 years.

1.2.3. Blackouts due to medical 
causes not covered in the standards
If the cause of the blackout is determined 
to be a medical condition not covered in 
the standards, then first principles regarding 
fitness to drive should be applied (refer to 
Part A section 2. Assessing fitness to drive 
– general guidance). Considerations include 
the likelihood of recurrence of blackout and 
the treatability of the condition as well as the 
nature of the driving task. There should also be 
an appropriate review period. A more stringent 
approach should be considered for commercial 
vehicle drivers.

1. AFTD2022-EXP-3a8e08652c83a2d0
Section 1.2.4 · PDF 69 · Printed page 58 · Original PDF
1.2.4. Blackouts of undetermined 
mechanism
If, despite extensive investigation, the 
mechanism of a blackout cannot be determined, 
fitness to drive should be assessed according 
to section 1.3. Medical standards for licensing. 
The standards for blackout of undetermined 
mechanism are similar to those for seizure.
2. AFTD2022-BLK-COM-004
Section 1.3 · PDF 70 · Printed page 59 · Original PDF
A person should not drive for 5 
years following a single blackout of 
undetermined nature.
A person should not drive for 10 years 
following two or more blackouts of 
undetermined nature separated by a 24-
hour period.
A person is not fit to hold an unconditional 
licence:
•	 if the person has experienced blackouts 
that cannot be diagnosed as syncope, 
seizure or another condition.
If there has been a single blackout or more 
than one blackout within a 24-hour period, 
a conditional licence may be considered 
by the driver licensing authority subject to 
at least annual review, taking into account 
information provided by an appropriate 
specialist as to whether the following 
criterion is met:
•	 there have been no further blackouts for 
at least 5 years.
3. AFTD2022-EXP-bbf242d555576d02
Section 1.3 · PDF 70 · Printed page 59 · Original PDF

4. AFTD2022-EXP-2332d9548f2abd01
Section 1.2.3 · PDF 68 · Printed page 57 · Original PDF
1.2.3. Blackouts due to medical 
causes not covered in the standards
If the cause of the blackout is determined 
to be a medical condition not covered in 
the standards, then first principles regarding 
fitness to drive should be applied (refer to 
Part A section 2. Assessing fitness to drive 
– general guidance). Considerations include 
the likelihood of recurrence of blackout and 
the treatability of the condition as well as the 
nature of the driving task. There should also be 
an appropriate review period. A more stringent 
approach should be considered for commercial 
vehicle drivers.

1. AFTD2022-EXP-3a8e08652c83a2d0
Section 1.2.4 · PDF 69 · Printed page 58 · Original PDF
1.2.4. Blackouts of undetermined 
mechanism
If, despite extensive investigation, the 
mechanism of a blackout cannot be determined, 
fitness to drive should be assessed according 
to section 1.3. Medical standards for licensing. 
The standards for blackout of undetermined 
mechanism are similar to those for seizure.
2. AFTD2022-BLK-COM-004
Section 1.3 · PDF 70 · Printed page 59 · Original PDF
A person should not drive for 5 
years following a single blackout of 
undetermined nature.
A person should not drive for 10 years 
following two or more blackouts of 
undetermined nature separated by a 24-
hour period.
A person is not fit to hold an unconditional 
licence:
•	 if the person has experienced blackouts 
that cannot be diagnosed as syncope, 
seizure or another condition.
If there has been a single blackout or more 
than one blackout within a 24-hour period, 
a conditional licence may be considered 
by the driver licensing authority subject to 
at least annual review, taking into account 
information provided by an appropriate 
specialist as to whether the following 
criterion is met:
•	 there have been no further blackouts for 
at least 5 years.
3. AFTD2022-EXP-bbf242d555576d02
Section 1.3 · PDF 70 · Printed page 59 · Original PDF
Commercial standards

A person should not drive for 5 
years following a single blackout of

A person should not drive for 10 years 
following two or more blackouts of 
undetermined nature separated by a 24-
hour period.
A person is not fit to hold an unconditional 
licence:
•	 if the person has experienced blackouts 
that cannot be diagnosed as syncope, 
seizure or another condition.
If there has been a single blackout or more 
than one blackout within a 24-hour period, 
a conditional licence may be considered 
by the driver licensing authority subject to

criterion is met:

at least 10 years.
4. AFTD2022-EXP-2332d9548f2abd01
Section 1.2.3 · PDF 68 · Printed page 57 · Original PDF
1.2.3. Blackouts due to medical 
causes not covered in the standards
If the cause of the blackout is determined 
to be a medical condition not covered in 
the standards, then first principles regarding 
fitness to drive should be applied (refer to 
Part A section 2. Assessing fitness to drive 
– general guidance). Considerations include 
the likelihood of recurrence of blackout and 
the treatability of the condition as well as the 
nature of the driving task. There should also be 
an appropriate review period. A more stringent 
approach should be considered for commercial 
vehicle drivers.

nature of the driving task. There should also be 
an appropriate review period. A more stringent 
approach should be considered for commercial 
vehicle drivers.

Where a person with one or more blackouts

While general standards allow for a conditional licence after 5 years, commercial standards (AFTD2022-EXP-bbf242d55576d02) impose stricter requirements. Specifically, a person is not fit to hold an unconditional licence if blackouts cannot be diagnosed as syncope, seizure, or another condition. The patient's diagnosis remains 'undetermined' (verified_patient_facts: blackout.diagnosis = 'undetermined').
